top_choice_rationale: Targeted protein degradation by induced proximity is a new, simple chemical principle supported by ternary-complex structures and degradation kinetics, with cereblon-based glue drugs already approved. Crews and Deshaies supply the concept and first demonstration, and Handa the cereblon mechanism, so one citation covers a coherent achievement within the three-laureate limit. P003 ranks second because it keeps the Crews and Deshaies core but drops the cereblon mechanism and adds base editing, which follows the 2020 CRISPR prize and rests on classical deamination chemistry. Perovskites follow, with a sound principle but a contested third name. Phase separation ranks below them because its in vivo scope is still debated. A prize is preferable to no award.
